name: browser-use
headline: Claude-Autopilot: Automate VS Code tasks
short_description: Claude-Autopilot is a VS Code/Cursor extension that automates Claude Code tasks. It features intelligent queuing, batch processing, and auto-resume. Developers benefit from streamlined workflows, reducing manual effort and improving productivity. The extension connects to VS Code and Cursor, enhancing the coding environment with AI-driven automation.
author: benbasha

sections.overview:
Claude Autopilot is a VS Code and Cursor extension that enables fully automated Claude Code task management. It queues hundreds of tasks for autonomous processing, automatically resuming work when Claude usage limits reset without manual intervention. The extension includes intelligent queue management, batch processing, sleep prevention to keep your computer awake during overnight runs, and comprehensive error recovery. Developers benefit from streamlined workflows that reduce manual effort, allowing tasks to complete unattended while you focus on other priorities. The extension offers both a native webview interface and mobile web access with real-time progress tracking and history browsing.
Queue 100+ coding tasks Friday evening for weekend processing
Automated overnight batch processing of Claude Code projects
Remote monitoring and control of Claude tasks via mobile web interface
Continuous task processing that auto-resumes after API limit resets
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/benbasha/Claude-Autopilot`
sections.usage:
```
Use the Claude-Autopilot VS Code extension to automate [SPECIFIC_TASK] for [PROJECT_NAME]. Focus on [KEY_OBJECTIVE] and ensure the process includes [CRITICAL_STEPS]. Monitor the extension's progress in the [OUTPUT_PANEL] and handle any errors by [ERROR_HANDLING_METHOD].
```
Copy

```
For the open-source project 'DataPulse', I used the Claude-Autopilot extension to automate the refactoring of legacy Python scripts. The task involved converting 45 scripts from Python 2.7 to Python 3.11, ensuring compatibility with modern libraries while preserving functionality. The extension processed the scripts in batches of 5, with intelligent queuing to avoid overwhelming system resources. It successfully refactored 32 scripts in the first pass, flagging 13 scripts for manual review due to deprecated syntax patterns like `print` statements without parentheses and `except Exception, e` clauses. The extension auto-resumed after I fixed the flagged issues, completing the refactoring in under 2 hours with zero manual intervention for the automated steps. The output panel showed real-time progress, including warnings for edge cases like mixed indentation and hardcoded file paths. Post-processing, I used the extension’s batch linting feature to verify all scripts passed PEP 8 compliance checks, saving an estimated 6 hours of manual work.
```
requirements: Claude Code or compatible AI agent
